items.title: Matrix-independent sublevel basin
items.note: For F : Vec n -> R convex with unique minimizer x* (hmin, huniq): F is coercive (Tendsto F (cocompact) atTop), every sublevel {F <= c} is compact; for every U in nhds x* there is eps > 0 with {F <= F(x*)+eps} contained in U, and every admissible run with F(x_0) <= F(x*)+eps stays in U (any H_0, which is a field of the run).

Corrected on 15 October 2026 (M39): end-of-proof mark. The library proof follows the paper (positive gap on a sphere, radial lower bound by convexity, ε = gap/2); it works in any finite-dimensional normed space, so with the sup norm of Vec n; the displays are stated with the Euclidean norm of the paper.

δ is a variable with defining equation δ = sInf {F(x*+u) − F(x*) : ‖u‖ = r} (Euclidean norm ‖euclideanVector u‖); the theorem proves that this infimum is a minimum (IsLeast) and is positive. Standing assumptions: the lemma's, U ∈ 𝓝 x*, r > 0 with the closed Euclidean ball B̄_r(x*) ⊆ U. The sphere is nonempty only for n ≥ 1: hn : 1 ≤ n is the article's convention (Definition art:admissible, n ≥ 1); the lemma's statement does not repeat it.
Under the assumptions of disp/001 (δ as defined there), for every x with ‖x − x*‖ ≥ r (Euclidean).

items.note: Stated under the hypotheses of Theorem art:polyhedral: near x* only cells containing x* occur, and the inward segment from a point of such a cell stays in it (inward_mem, local_cells_inward); the quadratic inward accuracy is display A/local/disp/004. "Without requiring BFGS to identify active manifolds" is a remark: the theorem's hypotheses concern only F.

PositivePartition.polyhedral is proved by the library's finite_polyhedral_basin → local_cells_basin, which follows this proof: discard the cells not containing x* and shrink (incident_neighborhood), radial derivative equality and local Taylor bounds give the inward condition on compact sets in the ball (local_cells_inward), then Lemma art:localization and the radial convergence corollary. Corrected on 15 October 2026 (M34, M38, M39): the radius of the common ball is ρ (B_ρ(x*); before B_r(x*), which clashed with the vector r_x = x − x* of global.tex); the inward condition holds "with M = Lρ² and θ = 1/2 for every band"; end-of-proof mark. The Lean statements write r for the radius and x − xstar for r_x.

Stated under the theorem's hypotheses plus the objects of local.tex:55-64 (the proof): the Euclidean ball B = B_ρ(x*) (hB; B_r(x*) before 15 October 2026, M38) with B ⊆ U and B ⊆ V_i for every cell containing x* (hBU, hBV), the discarded cells (hdisc: every cell meeting B contains x*), a common Lipschitz bound L ≥ 0 of the remaining extension gradients on B (hLip, Euclidean norms), a differentiability point x ∈ B with gradient g, and a cell P_i ∋ x. ∇f_i(x) is coordinateGradient (f i) x.

Corrected on 15 October 2026 (M38): Lρ² for Lr² (the radius is ρ). Same standing assumptions as disp/003, for 0 ≤ τ ≤ 1 (the inward segment of local.tex:63-64); ‖r_x‖² is sqNorm (x − xstar). The middle inequality is the sharp Taylor bound f(y) − f(x) − ∇f(x)^T(y−x) ≤ (L/2)‖y−x‖² for an L-Lipschitz gradient (taylor_upper_of_lipschitz, proved here; the library's taylor_remainder_le has the constant L instead of L/2).

items.title: Piecewise linear-quadratic and composite objectives
items.note: Piecewise linear-quadratic is the meaning fixed in the proof (local.tex:90-91): F(x) = x^T Q_i x + c_i^T x + d_i on each cell of a finite cover of ℝⁿ by closed full-dimensional polyhedra P_i = {x | a_ij^T x ≤ b_ij}. 'Has the local convergence property of Theorem art:polyhedral' is stated for every open neighborhood U of x* (the representation is global, so the theorem applies with any U): ∃ ε > 0, chosen before the run, with x_k ∈ U, F(x_k) → F(x*), x_k → x* for every admissible run with F(x_0) ≤ F(x*)+ε. plq is the first sentence; plq_loss_regularizer the second (loss convex and locally C^{1,1} on ℝⁿ, regularizer convex and PLQ, F = loss + reg with a unique minimizer). Full-dimensionality (_hfull) is not used.

Corrected on 15 October 2026 (M39): end-of-proof mark. The proof's sentence 'By piecewise linear-quadratic we mean ...' is a definition used in the statement of plq (see the corollary's note); quadratic_eq identifies the library's quadratic Q c d with x^TQx + c^Tx + d.

items.note: F_* is Fstar with IsLeast (Set.range F) Fstar (attained minimum). Hypothesis 1 is stated literally with frontier. Hypothesis 2 is stated literally (F is C² on an open neighborhood of p, or F = max{f₁,f₂} on an open neighborhood V of p where f₁, f₂ are convex and C² on V, both active at p, with linearly independent gradients); regular_of_paper converts it to the library's ContDiffAt ℝ 2 F p ∨ PlanarCornerCharts.ConvexTwoBranchRegularAt F p (paper_of_regular is the converse). The library proof differs from the paper's in the transport bookkeeping (|log λ_k| ≤ C d_k and a scalar energy instead of λ_k² ≤ 1 + L d_k); the paper's steps are covered by disp/007-009. items.title: Explicit convergence basin with curved, nonradial switching
items.note: f_i and F are variables with the defining equations of disp/009 (u = x 0, v = x 1); example_eq identifies them with PlanarQuadraticExample.branch/objective. The convergence part is the library's fullBFGS_explicit_basin, which applies the general planar theorem (planar_convergence_on_sublevel; its hypotheses hold for this F, see the non-vacuity example of the Local module). The failure part is stated explicitly: for every neighborhood N₀ of 0 there is η > 0 such that for every C some differentiable pair x, z ∈ N₀ with F(0)+η ≤ F(z) ≤ F(x), T = (h−g)^T(z−x) > 0 violates N² ≤ CT, N = (h−g)^T z (r_z = z, x* = 0); this negates (art:radial-condition) (A/global/disp/004) on N₀, for every C (not only C ≥ 0); the same pairs are eligible for c1 = 1/4, c2 = 1/2 (EligiblePair). The library's PlanarQuadraticSeparationTarget (planarQuadraticSeparation) also gives a realizing SPD H with bfgsStep H g 1 = z − x. Non-vacuity of the run part: PlanarQuadraticExample.nonradial_example_nonvacuous (bfgs_lean_article/BfgsArticle/AdmissibleRunExistence.lean, same hypotheses hf, hF) gives, for every H₀ ≻ 0 and all 0 < c₁ < c₂ < 1, an infinite admissible run with F(x₀) < 1/100 (x₀ = (1/1000, 0)) whose values and iterates converge to 0. It applies the general AdmissibleRunExistence.exists_admissible_run (convex, bounded below, differentiable at all but countably many points of every line through a point of differentiability, no point of differentiability with gradient zero).
The defining equations hf (f_0, f_1, f_2 in u = x 0, v = x 1) and hF (F = max_i f_i) of nonradial_example and of the display theorems of its proof.
